title: prefetch-hook-stale-config-incident-review
summary: During a regional configuration rollout a stale prefetch hook flag caused prefetching to be silently bypassed in one region, increasing tail latency and token cost for a subset of traffic. This doc captures detection, timeline, root cause, immediate mitigations, and longer-term action items.
symptoms_and_detection:
- p95 generation latency for model 'rwd-13b-quant' in europe-west-1 rose from ~160ms to ~380ms at 02:10 UTC.
- Error budget alert (slo-gen-p95-eu) fired at 02:18 UTC.
- Regional cost dashboard showed per-token GPU time increased by ~22% for eu-west-1 at 02:30 UTC.
- Oncall pager escalation triggered; oncall observed increased KV cache miss ratio and a drop in prefetch request counts to edge nodes.
timeline:
2025-01-12 01:50 UTC: infra/config-service triggered rollout of prefetch-policy change (validate->bypass) as part of emergency experiment rollout.
2025-01-12 02:05 UTC: rollout job started, targeting regions: us-central, europe-west-1, asia-south; staged percentage: 10% per region.
2025-01-12 02:09 UTC: rollout succeeded in us-central and asia-south. europe-west-1 rollout job completed but returned a 200 before post-apply verification; orchestrator marked region as 'applied'.
2025-01-12 02:10 UTC: first latency regression seen in europe-west-1; prefetch counts dropped ~95%.
2025-01-12 02:15 UTC: SRE oncall notified; investigation started (Marco).
2025-01-12 02:25 UTC: confirmed config difference: edge prefetch-hook flag was set to 'bypass' on routing proxies in eu-west-1; control plane still reported 'validate'.
2025-01-12 02:40 UTC: temporary rollback of the config assembly for europe-west-1 via infra service; traffic returned to normal over next 20 minutes.
2025-01-12 03:10 UTC: rollback confirmed and monitoring stabilized; incident declared mitigated.
2025-01-12 04:20 UTC: post-incident notes compiled and shared to SRE and runtime teams.
impact:
- Increased end-user p95 latency in europe-west-1 for ~2 hours (peak 380ms).
- Additional GPU time due to more repeated prefix computation: estimated +22% cost for impacted window.
- ~4% of live traffic routed through eu-west-1 experienced degraded latencies; no correctness or tokenization errors observed.
- No customer-facing errors logged; some customers reported slower responses.
root_cause:
A gap in the rollout verification path allowed a stale hook assembly to be applied at the edge. Specifically:
- The infra rollout job wrote the new prefetch-policy to the regional config store but the edge configuration agent reading that store performed a delta-merge using an out-of-date plugin manifest. The merge omitted the prefetch-hook key and left the node default as 'bypass'.
- The control plane's API responded with a 200 before the edge nodes completed plugin manifest reconcile, so the orchestrator marked the region as 'applied'.
- Lack of an end-to-end post-apply verification (prefetch-counts or kv-cache-miss-rate check) meant the misapplication was not detected by automated canaries.
immediate_mitigation:
- Rolled back the regional config assembly for europe-west-1 at 02:40 UTC via infra rollback endpoint.
- Increased monitoring alert sensitivity for kv-cache-miss-rate and prefetch-counts in all regions.
- Manual reconciliation of plugin manifests on a subset of affected edge nodes to ensure prefetch-hook key presence.
- Temporary hold on similar rollouts until verification gate added.
remediation:
- Add a post-apply verification step to the rollout orchestrator that validates prefetch-counts and kv-cache-miss-rate against expected baselines (small window sampling) before marking 'applied'.
- Enhance agent-side merge logic to fail loudly if expected keys from the new manifest are missing instead of silently preserving defaults.
- Backfill a small e2e test in the CI harness that simulates a manifest delta-merge and asserts prefetch-hook presence.
- Run a one-off audit of recent rollouts to identify other regions with similar plugin manifest age drift.
- Create a dashboard tile that surfaces config drift between control plane state and agent-reported state per region.
follow_up_actions: infra: add post-apply verification stage to rollout pipeline (JIRA-1256)
runtime: agent merge logic hard-fail on missing mandatory keys (PR #689)
sre: add kv-cache and prefetch canaries to global canary job (JIRA-1270)
observability: dashboard for control-plane vs agent-reported config parity (task obs-42)
runbook: update regional-rollout checklist to include 'manifest age check' and explicit preflight verification
lessons_learned:
- Silent default-preserving merges are high-risk for opinionated hooks (prefetch, kv-primer).
- Orchestrators must verify the runtime effect of a config change, not just the control-plane write success.
- Small staged rollouts can still leave a whole region degraded if agent reconciliation assumptions are wrong.
- Having a few lightweight behavioral canaries (prefetch-counts) catches a class of rollout mistakes earlier than latency SLOs alone.
oncall_notes:
- If you see a p95 spike in one region with no global pattern, check prefetch-counts and kv-cache-miss-rate first.
- Use infra rollback endpoint with region-scoped assembly id; don't rely on control-plane 'applied' flag alone.
- When running manual reconciliation: restart agent only after verifying plugin manifest file on disk and backing it up.
- If rollback incomplete, escalate to runtime-team Slack #runtime-ops and ping Marco and Evelyn.
